components.css: .ds-prov{--tint:var(--signal,#ffb020);display:grid;grid-template-columns:44px 1fr;gap:12px;align-items:center;padding:14px;border:1px solid var(--border,#232833);border-radius:6px;background:var(--surface,#12151b);color:var(--text,#eef1f5);transition:border-color .2s,background-color .2s}.ds-prov:hover{border-color:color-mix(in srgb,var(--tint) 45%,var(--border,#232833));background:var(--surface-2,#171b23)}.ds-mono{position:relative;display:grid;place-items:center;width:44px;height:44px;border-radius:11px;font:600 1rem 'Space Grotesk',sans-serif;border:1px solid color-mix(in srgb,var(--tint) 30%,var(--border-2,#313847));background:linear-gradient(160deg,color-mix(in srgb,var(--tint) 14%,var(--surface,#12151b)),var(--bg,#0a0c10))}.ds-mono::after{content:'';position:absolute;top:6px;right:6px;width:5px;height:5px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--tint)}.ds-prov b{font:600 .95rem 'Space Grotesk',sans-serif;display:block}.ds-prov small{font:.6875rem 'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;letter-spacing:.06em;color:var(--text-dim,#8a94a4)}.ds-prov ul{grid-column:1/-1;display:flex;gap:6px;list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0}.ds-prov li{font:.6875rem 'IBM Plex Mono',monospace;padding:3px 9px;border-radius:999px;border:1px solid var(--border-2,#313847);color:var(--text-muted,#99a3b3)}.ds-prov li em{font-style:normal}.ds-prov li.is-auto{border-color:color-mix(in srgb,var(--signal,#ffb020) 40%,var(--border,#232833))}.ds-prov li.is-auto em{color:var(--signal,#ffb020)}

narrative.overview:
The site is not a page about Kongtrol; it is a guest session inside Kongtrol's control tower (ssh guest@kongtrol.tower). Everything a visitor reads arrives as terminal output: a "Last login" line, a block-letter ASCII banner, # comments, commands with $, tunnel rows with ✔, navigation written as CLI flags (--inicio, --guia) and a tmux status bar pinned to the bottom with numbered windows (0:motd, 1:empezar…), the kill-switch state (armed) and a clock. Plain-language sentences (Inter) sit inside that session so non-technical visitors are never left decoding jargon; the terminal is the frame, not a test.

The material is amber phosphor on near-black in the dark theme and ink on bone paper in the light theme, with a faint field of concentric contour rings echoing the monkey mark's line art. Density is calm: one terminal window per screen, generous section rhythm, no decorative imagery. Motion is reserved for things that explain: the boot timeline, the routing diagram, the attach demo, the theme wipe. Components themselves stay precise and quiet.
keyCharacteristics: Terminal session as the page frame (window chrome, ASCII banner, tmux bar, CLI-flag navigation).
One brand accent (amber signal); every other color is a state.
Three type voices: Space Grotesk headings, Inter prose, IBM Plex Mono for everything machine-like.
Two complete themes (follows the OS preference until the visitor picks one; light on bone paper) plus a hidden green-phosphor CRT mode (↑↑↓↓←→←→BA).

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Amber is the only brand color. If something is amber, it is the brand or the action; it is never a state.

rules.name: The Green Means Up Rule
rules.body: Green means up or OK: a connected or healthy tunnel, a passed check (✔ in terminal output), the attach demo's "Conectado". Groups, categories, "auto" support and decoration never use green.

rules.name: The Four States Rule
rules.body: Connected = green, connecting = steel, no response = caution orange, error = red. Each state also carries a word or icon; color is never the only signal.

rules.name: The Machine Speaks Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything a computer would print or accept — commands, flags, paths, IPs, filenames, states — is set in IBM Plex Mono. Sentences meant for people are Inter.

rules.name: The 11px Floor Rule
rules.body: No rendered text below 11px, on any screen size (ADR-0028).

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Only the terminal window floats; everything else gains depth through tone or responds to interaction.

dos: Do keep amber as the only accent and use it for the one primary action per section.
Do use green only for "connected" or a passed check, caution orange for "no response", red for errors, steel for "connecting", always with a word or icon.
Do write anything machine-like in IBM Plex Mono and anything for people in Inter.
Do keep motion for demos that explain (routing, attach, boot) and animate only transform/opacity, on screen, respecting reduced motion.
Do keep the terminal frame (window chrome, ASCII banner, CLI-flag nav, tmux bar) when adding sections.
donts: Don't use green for groups, categories, support levels or decoration.
Don't use amber to signal a state; it collides with the brand and the primary button.
Don't add glow, float or breathing effects to buttons and cards; expression belongs to the demos.
Don't render text below 11px or targets below 24px.
Don't use third-party VPN logos or brand colors.
Don't add shadows to anything except the terminal window and the primary button hover.
